title: Phones
intro: With the DBine app on your phone you see the locks and running queries of your connections and, if you allow it, end a session, without being at the computer. Connections and their passwords never leave this computer: the phone asks DBine and DBine answers.
allowHelp: While on, DBine listens on the local network for paired phones. It works with DBine open and the phone on the same network.
portHelp: The port DBine uses to serve phones.
canKill: Can end sessions and cancel queries
canKillHelp: Ending a session, cancelling a query and running a task are enabled per phone, and the phone confirms them every time with fingerprint, face or PIN. The phone notifies you when a query that took more than 10 seconds finishes and when a scheduled task fails or has an alert (according to its «Notify» setting): with the app open, right away; with the app closed, every 15 minutes.
removeConfirm: Remove “{{name}}”? It's disconnected now and has to be paired again to use it.
scan: Scan it with your phone's camera or from the DBine app (Pair). If you don't have the app yet, the code takes you to download it.
expires: The code expires in {{seconds}} s and works for a single phone.
sameNetwork: If the phone is on another network, it connects over the internet according to “Outside the local network”.
askText: “{{name}}” wants to pair with this computer.
askCompare: Check that the phone shows this same code:
remoteHelp: How the phone reaches this computer when it isn't on the same network. Everything travels end-to-end encrypted with the keys from the QR code: the relay server only sees unreadable data.
publicHelp: iroh tries to connect directly; if the networks don't allow it, it goes through n0's public servers (free, with no availability guarantee). They see the IPs and the traffic volume, never the content.
ownHelp: The URL of your iroh-relay server (https), one per line. Only that server is used: nothing goes through third-party servers. Phones already paired get the change on their next connection.
publicConfirm:
When the phone can't connect directly, the connection will go through iroh's public servers, operated by a third party (n0).

What they see: the IP addresses of this computer and of the phone, and when and how much traffic goes through.
What they don't see: the content. Everything is end-to-end encrypted with the keys from the QR code; they can't read or modify anything.

Your databases' connections and passwords never leave this computer, and the phone can't run free-form queries.

If you don't want a third party in the middle, use your own server or keep local network only.
